name: doc2video

tools.name: d2v_connect_account
tools.description: Connect this server to the user's doc2video account. Call it first when other tools say the user is not logged in. It returns a link: ask the user to open it, sign in or sign up, and click Approve, then call this tool again to finish.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for approval on this call (default 30)

tools.name: d2v_list_projects
tools.description: List the user's doc2video projects (id, name, status, format).

tools.name: d2v_get_project
tools.description: Full project detail: settings, sources, every scene (narration, visual mode, photo, keyframe URL), jobs, preview/final video, cost estimate and suggested next steps.

project.description: Project id, 8-character id prefix, or exact project name

tools.name: d2v_list_voices
tools.description: Narrator voices available for projects.

tools.name: d2v_create_project
tools.description: Create a video project from local files and folders (uploaded from this machine), public links, written text, or an AI draft prompt. Photos (jpg/png/webp/heic) are featured in scenes; documents (pdf/docx/pptx/md/txt/csv/json) supply the story. Set build: true to start generating the storyboard right away (then poll d2v_wait).

sources.description: Absolute paths of local files or folders to upload, or public http(s) links to documents, photos or web pages

text.description: Written content to use as a source

draft_prompt.description: Have AI write the source content from this description

build.description: Start the storyboard pipeline immediately (default false)

use_credits.description: Pay from the user's credits when the call needs it: $0.50 for a storyboard beyond today's free ones, or AI clips beyond what the purchase covers (the credits_confirm_required error says how much). Only set true after the user agreed to spend that amount.

duration_seconds.description: Target length in seconds; 0 = AI picks from the content

creative_direction.description: Tone, visual style, focus, audience, things to avoid

voice.description: Narrator voice name or id (see d2v_list_voices)

consistency.description: Keep characters/style consistent by referencing earlier keyframes (default on)

photo_treatment.description: How user photos become visuals: original = the photo itself, restyle = AI-enhanced from the photo

contact_email.description: Shown in the closing call to action

instructions:
doc2video turns the user's documents and photos into a narrated, AI-produced video.

Typical flow:
0. If a tool says the user is not logged in, call d2v_connect_account, give the user the link it
   returns (they sign in or sign up and click Approve), then call it again to finish.
1. d2v_create_project with the user's local folder/files in `sources` (photos are featured in scenes,
   documents supply the story) and build: true. Ask about length (duration_seconds), orientation
   (aspect_ratio) and tone (creative_direction) if the user hasn't said.
2. The storyboard builds on the server (script → keyframes → narration → preview) over several
   minutes. Call d2v_wait repeatedly until done is true.
3. d2v_view_storyboard to see the keyframe images and narration, then summarize for the user and
   share the preview_url. Steer with d2v_regenerate_keyframe, d2v_update_narration and
   d2v_update_scene, then d2v_run_step step=preview to refresh the preview video.
4. Final production costs money: show d2v_estimate_cost and let the user decide. Only call
   d2v_create_checkout_link (the user pays in their browser), d2v_unlock_with_credits,
   d2v_redeem_promo_code or d2v_produce_video when the user asks. Then d2v_wait and d2v_download_video.

Free allowance: 2 storyboards and 20 scene redos per day on unpaid projects. A further storyboard
costs $0.50 of prepaid credits: tools return credits_confirm_required — ask the user, and only with
their OK call again with use_credits: true. d2v_get_credits shows the balance; d2v_add_credits_link
lets the user top up in their browser.

A purchase covers the project at the price paid. AI clips beyond that — a pricier engine chosen
after buying, or a new take of a clip that's already made — are paid from credits the same way
(credits_confirm_required says how much). Retrying a failed clip is free.

Projects can be referenced by id, 8-character id prefix, or exact name; scenes by number.
